sections.subhead: Stay involved. Give back. Join the crew.
paragraphs: Officiating is a way to stay connected to the sports you love, meet great people, stay active, earn some extra money, and give back to the athletes, schools, and families in your community.
Maybe you played. Maybe you coached. Maybe your kids played. Or maybe you've simply loved sports your whole life.
Whatever brought you to the game, officiating gives you another way to be part of it.
Greater Naples Officials Association recruits, trains, and supports new and experienced officials throughout Naples, Collier County, and Southwest Florida.

sections.heading: There's Still a Place for You in the Game
sections.tagline: You don't have to be playing or coaching to stay involved in sports.
sections.intro: Officials are an important part of what makes local games possible. You get a different view of the game, a new challenge, and a chance to become part of a community of people who enjoy sports just as much as you do.

items.title: Stay Connected
items.text: Keep participating in the sports that have been part of your life.

items.title: Join a Great Group of People
items.text: Work alongside officials from different backgrounds who share a love of sports and enjoy being part of a crew.

items.title: Stay Active
items.text: Officiating keeps you moving, thinking, and engaged.

items.title: Make Some Extra Money
items.text: Work games around your availability and earn additional income doing something you enjoy.

items.title: Give Back
items.text: Help local athletes, schools, leagues, and families continue playing the games they work hard to prepare for.

sections.intro: Start with the sport you know, the sport you played or coached, or simply the one you enjoy most.

sections.heading: Never Officiated Before?
paragraphs: You don't need previous officiating experience to get started. Nobody expects you to know every rule, signal, position, or mechanic on day one.
GNOA helps new officials learn what they need to know and connects them with experienced officials who remember exactly what it felt like to work their first game.

items: And most importantly, you'll learn by doing.

image.alt: Veteran official mentoring a younger official on the field

sections.heading: You Become Part of a Community
lines: One of the best parts of officiating is the people you meet.
You'll work games with people from different professions, different ages, and different backgrounds, all connected by the same thing: They enjoy sports.
You'll prepare together. Work games together. Talk about plays afterward.
Help newer officials. Learn from experienced officials.
And probably share plenty of laughs along the way.
For many officials, the friendships and camaraderie become just as important as the games.

image.alt: Group of smiling GNOA officials in caps taking a selfie together before a night game

blocks.p: Games don't happen without people willing to officiate them.
Athletes prepare. Coaches prepare. Schools and families show up.
But somebody still has to step onto the field, court, or mat and help make the competition possible.
Officiating is a practical way to give something back to your community.

You're helping local athletes compete. You're helping schools and programs play their schedules. And you're helping make sure the next generation gets the same opportunity to enjoy sports that you did.
Officiating is flexible, and you can block off dates when you're unavailable and work around your schedule.
Games are typically played on weekday evenings and Saturdays, with no Sunday games.
For many officials, it fits alongside work, family, travel, and other commitments.

sections.heading: Training & Support
lines: Good officials aren't expected to figure everything out on their own.
GNOA provides pre-season and in-season training opportunities for each sport to help officials prepare, review rules and mechanics, ask questions, and continue learning throughout the season.
Development isn't only about moving to a higher level.

Sometimes getting better means communicating more clearly, being in a better position, handling a difficult situation better, helping a newer official, or simply becoming more comfortable and confident in your role.

image.alt: Group of officials in striped shirts talking before a game

sections.heading: Already an Experienced Official?
sections.subhead: Come join the crew in Southwest Florida.
paragraphs: If you're relocating to Naples, Collier County, or the surrounding area, or simply looking for a new association, we'd like to hear from you.
Tell us which sport you officiate and a little about your experience. We'll connect you with the appropriate GNOA leadership and help you understand the local process.
sections.after: More than anything, we're looking for good people who enjoy sports and want to be part of the officiating community.

image.alt: Four experienced officials in a pregame huddle on the field

blocks.p: Every sport has its own uniform and equipment requirements, but don't rush out and buy everything before talking with GNOA.
We'll help you understand what you actually need and what can wait.
Experienced officials may also have used, extra, or hand-me-down equipment available for someone just getting started.
Talk to us first. See what's available. Buy what you need.
